doctrine: Numbers below are SEALED snapshots. The telemetry script MUST surface provenance + epistemic_class + as_of per field. Updating this file is a F13 sovereign action; script MUST NOT mutate. epistemic_class: OBS = observation (measured/surveyed), DER = derivation (computed from OBS), INT = interpretation (judgment, not measured). All sources carry epistemic_class tagging.
changelog_v3: Added Ilham Centre OBS (n=1,002, 3.1% MoE, Jul 18-30), Ong Kian Ming INT structural model (Jul 27), early voting OBS turnout data (91.06%), Ilham 7-reason qualitative framework, post-poll audit protocol, and expanded battleground seat signals (7 seats from 3). Sovereign confidence raised from 65%→72% on converging multi-source evidence.

VODUS_N9_N437.methodology_ref: Vodus OMTOS online survey, weighted to NS ethnic/age/gender demographics
VODUS_N9_N437.note: n=437 is below conventional 1,000 margin-of-error threshold; treat as directional proxy, not definitive estimate.

ILHAM_N9_N1002.methodology_ref: Stratified random sampling across all 36 DUN, covering ethnicity/gender/age/education/income/occupation/locality. Quantitative statistical + qualitative thematic analysis. Includes SPR 2022/2023 scoresheet cross-referencing.
ILHAM_N9_N1002.note: Most rigorous publicly available dataset for N9 PRN16. n=1,002 with 3.1% MoE at 95% confidence. Fieldwork through final campaign week.

ONG_KIAM_MING_STRUCTURAL_2026_07_27.analyst: Dr Ong Kian Ming (former Bangi MP, political economist)
ONG_KIAM_MING_STRUCTURAL_2026_07_27.methodology_ref: Seat-level ethnic composition model: Malay turnout 80%, Chinese 65%, Indian 60%, Others 65%. Vote transfer estimates between BN-PN pact partners. 2022 GE15 state-seat results as baseline. 10 battleground seats identified.
ONG_KIAM_MING_STRUCTURAL_2026_07_27.note: Most detailed published seat-level model. Structural rather than polling-based. Ong predicted Johor outcome correctly (BN landslide). His N9 model projects BN-PN 23-25 seats.

EARLY_VOTING_SPR_2026_07_28.note: Early voting exceeded SPR's 90% target. High security-force turnout historically correlates with higher overall turnout and traditionally favors BN (discipline vote).

SOVEREIGN_PROJECTION_2026_07_31_FINAL.rationale_ref: Seven-source convergence: Ilham Centre (n=1,002) + Ong Kian Ming structural model + Vodus (n=437) + Ilham 7-reason qual framework + Johor momentum spillover + early voting 91% turnout + Bersatu structural spoiler effect. PH's mixed-seat dependency collapsing. Non-Malay turnout is single largest uncertainty.
SOVEREIGN_PROJECTION_2026_07_31_FINAL.note: F13 sovereign agentic synthesis. Confidence upgraded from 65% to 72% on converging multi-source evidence. Ilham Centre n=1,002 is the strongest signal.

ILHAM_SEVEN_REASONS.source: Ilham Centre via Sinar Harian / Astro Awani
seven_reasons: Kombinasi BN-PN mencipta gelombang Melayu-Islam lebih besar berbanding Johor — identity politics driving turnout
Perpindahan undi lebih berkesan antara penyokong BN dan PN — vote transfer efficiency exceeding 70%
Kempen PH hilang punca — mesej tidak sampai ke pengundi Melayu luar bandar
Pengundi Cina tidak lagi memberi sokongan automatik kepada PH — cooling enthusiasm, driven by absence of alternatives rather than confidence
MB Aminuddin Harun tenggelam — 32% favourability vs Johor MB Onn Hafiz 58%; leadership vacuum at campaign peak
Perubahan sikap pengundi muda daripada personaliti calon kepada parti — candidate-centric → party-centric loyalty
Pengundi India menjauhi PH — former strongholds showing erosion; Seremban Jaya (27.9% Indian) is key monitor
ILHAM_SEVEN_REASONS.note: Qualitative framework explaining the mechanism behind quantitative projections. Each reason maps to specific seat dynamics.

constituency_forecast_vodus.note: Vodus: BN has 15 CLEAR leads vs PH 9, but PH ahead in 8 of 10 closely contested seats, raising PH projected total to 17.

constituency_forecast_ilham_n1002.note: Ilham Centre final projection. If BN captures some tossups, BN-PN reaches 2/3 majority. All 5 tossups are DAP-held seats being challenged by BN (MCA).

bersatu_seats_independent.note: Bersatu contesting under own logo, excluded from BN-PN seat pact. Clashes with former PN allies in 8 constituencies. Structural split benefits PH in marginals. Analysts expect Bersatu to lose all seats but could win Labu (N20).

mb_favourability_gap.source: Vodus Research favourability survey (referenced in multiple reports)
mb_favourability_gap.note: Johor comparison: Onn Hafiz 58% favourability → BN won 48/56. Aminuddin 32% → significant leadership perception gap.

sovereign_coalition_forecast.confidence_upgrade_rationale: Ilham Centre n=1,002 (3.1% MoE) provides strongest single OBS signal. Converging with Ong's structural model, Vodus directional survey, early voting data, and Ilham's 7-reason qualitative framework. Seven independent sources point BN-PN 19-24 seats.
sovereign_coalition_forecast.confidence_delta_note: Remaining 28% uncertainty allocated to: non-Malay turnout variance (12%), Bersatu spoiler magnitude in marginals (8%), PH ground machinery last-mile (5%), adat/royal dampening effect (3%).

post_poll_audit_protocol.trigger_time: After 10pm MYT 2026-08-01 when SPR announces first batch
post_poll_audit_protocol.validation_criteria: BN-PN ≥ 19 seats = model validated. PH ≥ 16 seats = model failed.

seats.name: Linggi
seats.note: MB Aminuddin (PH-PKR) moved from Sikamat vs BN incumbent Mohd Faizal + Bersatu Zamri. 3-cornered. 61.8% Malay. 50-year UMNO fortress. Aminuddin self-assessed 50-50. Ilham Centre: too close BN-lean. Ong: BN wins. Bersatu candidate may eat 5-8% anti-establishment vote, helping BN retain.

seats.name: Sikamat
seats.note: Aminuddin vacated after 4 terms (since 2008). PKR's Nor Azman (political secretary) vs BN Shahrul Nizam vs Bersatu Tun Faisal. 71.6% Malay. Without Aminuddin personal vote, structural Malay consolidation dominates. Ong: PN wins. PKR machine untested without MB brand.

seats.name: Ampangan
seats.note: 329-vote PKR majority in 2023 (2.2%). 72.8% Malay. 3-cornered: PH(PKR) vs PN(PAS-Mohamad Rafie, comeback bid) vs Bersatu. B40 cost-of-living at peak. Ong: PN wins. Ilham: BN-PN advantage. Anti-incumbency + PAS grassroots in Seremban periphery.

seats.name: Klawang
seats.note: AMANAH's Bakri Sawir defending. Margin shrunk from 11.7% (2018) to 6.4% (2023). 3-cornered vs PN(Wawasan-Danni Rais, cousin) vs Bersatu. Former Bersatu candidate now on Wawasan ticket creates voter confusion. Ilham: too close. Ong: PN wins. If AMANAH loses all 7 contests, party wiped from N9.

seats.name: Serting
seats.note: PAS incumbent vs PH vs Bersatu. Bersatu fielding Affendy Salleh against PAS candidate. Split opposition vote magnitude uncertain. Ilham: too close. Ong: PN retains. If Bersatu eats >8% of PAS vote, PH wins with <40%. Complex 3-body problem.

seats.name: Bagan Pinang
seats.note: PAS incumbent (3,426 majority). Army camp seat + resort tourism. 3-cornered: PAS vs PH vs Bersatu. Military postal vote + BN-PN consolidation favors BN reclaiming. If BN wins, validates discipline-vote hypothesis. Moderate Bersatu spoiler effect expected.

seats.name: Chennah
seats.note: Loke (DAP SG) vs MCA's Siow Kong Choon. 48% Malay, 7% Orang Asli. Ilham: too close. Loke holds if non-Malay turnout >65% and OA don't swing heavily BN. Ong: too close, slight BN advantage if MCA announces exco offer for Siow. DAP machine strongest here.

seats.name: Nilai
seats.note: DAP held since 2008 (10,889 majority). 5-cornered fight. Ilham: too close. Losing grip due to Chinese voter cooling and Indian community swing. MCA mounting strongest challenge in decade. Young urban voters focused on jobs/housing.

seats.name: Temiang
seats.note: DAP held 4 terms since 2008 (34.1% margin in 2023). Ilham: too close. MCA chief Leaw Kok Chan challenging. After MCA won 8 seats in Johor (surpassing DAP's 6), Temiang tests whether MCA resurgence reaches N9. DAP newcomer Ho Weng Wah (Loke's political sec) defending.

seats.name: Repah
seats.note: DAP held since 2013 (5,950 majority). Ilham: too close. BN fielding MCA's Koh Kim Swee. Tampin town mixed seat. Chinese turnout critical — if below 60%, seat becomes vulnerable.

seats.name: Labu
seats.note: 3-cornered: Bersatu(incumbent Hanifah, N9 Bersatu chief) vs PH(PKR) vs BN(UMNO). Bersatu's best individual chance to win a seat. Won with 1,640 majority in 2023. If Bersatu wins Labu + 1 more, becomes kingmaker in hung assembly scenario.

seats.name: Rantau
seats.note: Tok Mat (BN deputy chairman) defending 7th term. Straight fight vs young doctor Azizul Hakim (PH). 10,280 majority in 2023 (72% vote share). Margin shrinkage is the signal — if <60%, BN brand softening in traditional heartlands. If >70%, BN momentum confirmed.

render_hints.voter_turnout_projection_source: Historical N9 turnout ~74% + Merdeka Center trackers + Johor 2026 comparison (69.6% Johor, N9 expected higher due to Klang Valley commuter proximity)
